note: Both sets capture the main operating values (design-point CP = 0.489 and CT = 0.804, 15 MW rated power, 20 MN-m rated torque, TSR 20→3, blade pitch 0→22°) and both repeat the same misread of the right-axis tick 2.25 as a rotor-thrust value at 10 m/s. Set B is the cleaner set: it binds Cp ≈ 0.5 to the Region 2 plateau (7–10 m/s) instead of a single wind speed, reads rotor thrust at 25 m/s as 0.9 MN (closer to the curve) rather than 1.0 MN, and repeats each fact far less often. Set A states the same facts up to three times (rated torque, TSR at 3 m/s, design-point CP, blade pitch 0° in Region 2) and gives mutually inconsistent rotor-thrust values at 10 m/s (2.8 and 2.25 MN).
remarks: Both extractions read the right-axis gridline label 2.25 in panel (b) as a data value for rotor thrust at 10 m/s; the actual thrust there is near the curve peak (~2.6–2.8 MN at the Region 2/3 boundary ~10.5 m/s), so the 2.7/2.8 MN claims are also only approximate. Both give Power Coef. ≈ 0.1 at ~17 m/s, which looks too low (the curve is nearer 0.2 there). Most quotes are bare axis labels and do not support the numeric values claimed — a systemic weakness of chart extraction in both sets. Both sets also omit the rated/region-boundary wind speed (~10.5 m/s) that conditions most of these plateaus.
